If you haven't seen a total differential before. Think of it this way.
Suppose \( x \) and \( y \) are functions of \( t \). Apply chain rule to both sides of (**) to get:
\[
f_{x} \cdot \frac{d x}{d t}+f_{y} \cdot \frac{d y}{d t}=0
\]

s057_eq_shape8.png.text:
Now multiply both sides by differential \( d t \) to get:
\[
f_{x} \cdot d x+f_{y} \cdot d y=0
\]
